title: Even after Easter the Apostles were slow — but those mysteries are written in the NT
source_text: IV. Et certe quod discipuli ista tum non intelligebant, inde manifestum est, quod, etiam postquam Christum a mortuis excitatum viderunt, nesciebant tamen quae futura esset regni ipsius natura; quam suam ignorantiam produnt illa ad Christum quaestione, quae a Luca refertur cap. 1. Actorum, Domine, num hoc tempore restitues regnum Israel? Imo post ipsam Christi ascensionem, Gentium vocatio, & cum populo Dei in unum corpus collectio a Petro non satis intelligebatur, donec de mysterio isto, speciali visione plenius edoceretur, ut videre est Actorum capit. 10. Multa vero illa Christus proculdubio Apostolos docuit, tum viva voce post resurrectionem, tum per Spiritum sanctum abundanter illis superfusum post sessionem ad dexteram Patris. Sed unde Pontificii probant, aut conjiciunt illa scripta non esse, cum mysteria ista quae breviter recensuimus, & longe plura, scripta reperiantur in Evangelistarum scriptis, quae illi proculdubio a Magistro suo hauserant? Itaque, verum est quidem Christum ante mortem habuisse multa dicenda discipulis quae illi ferre non poterant, & verum quoque Christum illa discipulis suis dixisse & aperuisse post resurrectionem. At falsum est ista non fuisse scripta ab Apostolis & Evangelistis, saltem quoad summam atque substantiam, & quantum nobis ad salutem satis est. Sunt enim illa ipsa mysteria quae per totum Novum Testamentum sparsa sunt. Nec adversarii possunt contrarium ullo argumento probare.
pass_a_gloss: And certainly that the disciples then did not understand those things is manifest from this, that even after they saw Christ raised from the dead, they still did not know what the nature of his kingdom would be; which ignorance of theirs they show by that question to Christ which is reported by Luke in Acts chapter 1, Lord, will you at this time restore the kingdom to Israel? Nay after Christ ascension itself, the calling of the Gentiles, and their gathering with the people of God into one body, was not sufficiently understood by Peter until he was more fully taught about that mystery by a special vision, as is to be seen in Acts chapter 10. But those many things Christ without doubt taught the Apostles, both by living voice after the resurrection, and through the Holy Spirit abundantly poured out upon them after the sitting at the right hand of the Father. But whence do the Pontificians prove, or conjecture, that those things were not written, when those mysteries which we have briefly reviewed, and far more, are found written in the writings of the Evangelists, which they without doubt had drawn from their Master? Therefore it is indeed true that Christ before death had many things to say to the disciples which they could not bear, and it is also true that Christ said and opened those things to his disciples after the resurrection. But it is false that those things were not written by the Apostles and Evangelists, at least as to the sum and substance, and as much as is enough for us for salvation. For they are those very mysteries which are scattered through the whole New Testament. Nor can the adversaries prove the contrary by any argument.
pass_b_english: Acts 1 proves the point: even after Easter they still asked about restoring Israel kingdom.
Peter needed Acts 10 vision before Gentile inclusion clicked.
Christ did teach after the resurrection and by the poured-out Spirit — true.
False: that teaching stayed unwritten; the NT already holds those mysteries in substance for salvation.
